Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

VP of Quantum - Diasense ApS

Reports to: Marvin Holten, Founder and CTO

Team: Quantum Lead, Quantum Engineers, and part-time specialists in quantum information science and quantum optics, growing through 2027

Location: Quantum Denmark, Copenhagen, Denmark. On-site.

Start: January 2027

Company Overview

Diasense is a deep-tech company turning fundamental quantum physics into world-class scientific instruments. We are building the world's most sensitive magnetic microscope, using nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond to measure magnetic fields at a sensitivity that no other technique can reach.

We are applying that instrument to one of the hardest measurement problems in semiconductor manufacturing: seeing what is actually happening inside a finished chip, electrically and non-destructively. It is a market where the physics has to be exceptional and the engineering has to be industrial, and very few companies in the world are attempting both.

We are a spin-out of DTU Physics, based in the quantum center of Copenhagen, and we are about to move from a working prototype to instruments installed at customers’ sites. The team today is eight full-time and six part-time people. Over 2027 and 2028, we are building that to around thirty. By joining now, you will be one of the people who decide what this company becomes, not someone who inherits it.

Position Overview

Job Description

We are looking for the person who will own the quantum side of our instrument, outright.

You will lead our quantum function: a Quantum Lead, quantum engineers, and part-time specialists, growing over the next eighteen months. You are an experimentalist at heart. We are not looking for someone who manages a lab from a desk. We are looking for the person other physicists go to when something does not work, and nobody can say why. Today that person is our CTO, and your role is to change that. When the quantum work gets stuck, it should stop with you.

You will be joining at the transition point where the instrument moves from lab to customer sites. The physics has to keep improving, and it now also has to withstand contact with the real world. Both halves of that are yours.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Ownership of the Quantum Platform

• 
Own the performance of the NV-diamond measurement chain end to end: optical read-out, microwave control, sensitivity, noise floor and measurement protocols.

• 
Set the technical direction for how we push sensitivity and measurement speed over the next two years.

• 
Make the calls on where the physics effort goes, and be accountable for them.

Hands-on Experimental Work

• 
Spend the majority of your week in the lab, on the instrument, with your hands on it.

• 
Diagnose and fix the problems that have no procedure attached - the ones where the measurement is wrong and nobody yet knows why.

• 
Develop and prove new experimental protocols, rather than reviewing someone else's.

Leading and Building the Quantum Team

• 
Lead the quantum function: our Quantum Lead, quantum engineers and part-time academic specialists, with further hires planned through 2027.

• 
Raise what the team can do unaided. Success looks like fewer problems reaching you over time, not more.

• 
Own hiring for the quantum team as it grows, together with the CTO.

Instruments in the Field

• 
Take technical responsibility for the quantum performance of instruments installed at customer sites.

• 
Support and eventually supervise measurement campaigns at customer locations, so that deployment does not depend on the founders.

• 
Work closely with instrumentation, software and applications colleagues - this instrument only works when all four disciplines agree.

Qualifications & Experience

• 
A PhD in Physics, Quantum Optics, Atomic Physics or a closely related field, followed by substantial further experimental experience in academia or industry.

• 
Deep, sustained, hands-on experimental physics. Years at the bench, building and debugging experiments yourself. This is the single most important qualification and we will test for it.

• 
A demonstrable record of solving unfamiliar, hard experimental problems without supervision. We are interested in what you did when the standard approach failed.

• 
Experience guiding, mentoring or leading other researchers or engineers - formally or informally. You do not need to have held a management title, but you do need to want this half of the job.

• 
An inquisitive and stubborn mindset: willing to question assumptions, including your own, and to keep going after a problem that has already resisted three attempts.

• 
Fluency in Python or MATLAB for research-grade data analysis.

Experience with one or more of the following is a significant advantage:

• 
Cold atoms or trapped ions. Our techniques originate in cold-atom physics rather than in quantum sensing, and we have found that people trained in that tradition tend to carry exactly the debugging instinct this role needs.

• 
Magnetometry, especially with NV centres, and precision measurements.

• 
Microwave electronics and real-time control systems.

• 
Building complex free-space optical systems from components.

• 
Taking a laboratory technique out of the laboratory.

Compensation & Benefits

• 
A competitive salary package.

• 
An attractive warrant package. You will share directly in what you build, and at this stage the share is meaningful.

• 
Relocation support for you and your family, and assistance with the Danish researcher tax scheme, which for qualifying international hires taxes salary at a flat 32.84 percent for up to seven years.

• 
Denmark's quantum ecosystem at your door: DTU Physics, the Niels Bohr Institute and one of Europe's densest concentrations of quantum research.

• 
A small, senior team where decisions are made in a conversation rather than in a process.

USP's for this job

• 
You are the ceiling, not waiting for one. In most companies, the deepest technical authority sits above you, and you work within it. Here you are being hired to become it. The quantum direction of this instrument will be yours.

• 
Lead a team without leaving the lab. Almost every physicist who moves into leadership loses the bench. This role is explicitly designed so that you do not - the leadership comes from being the best experimentalist, not from stopping being one.

• 
Build the Unprecedented: You will be a leading the development and rollout of the most powerful magnetic microscope in the world, directly pushing the boundaries of scientific measurement.

• 
It leaves the building. Our instruments are going into customer laboratories. You will see your work measured by whether it survives in somebody else's fab, which is a rarer and more satisfying test than a paper.

• 
Early enough to matter. Fourteen people today, around thirty by the end of 2028. The people joining now set how this company works.

Company Description

With more than 2,700 employees, Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit & Assurance, Tax & Legal, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, Technology, and Transformations.

About the team

In Organization and Work Transformation, we help clients achieve their transformation goals through their most valuable asset: their people. Successful transformation relies on defining the right organization, operations, and behaviours, and anchoring changes with employees' collaboration. Our consultants translate transformation agendas into new operating, capability, and governance models. We design and implement strategic change initiatives based on data-driven insights, enhancing organizational performance, productivity, and profitability. If you are passionate about this work and value collaboration, challenging the status quo, and personal development, this position is for you!

Job Description

Join Deloitte's Organization and Work Transformation team as a Consultant and contribute to meaningful change for our clients. We are looking for motivated professionals with experience supporting change management and organizational readiness in ERP and technology implementation programs. As a Consultant, you will work alongside industry experts, utilize advanced methodologies, and help shape the future of organizations. If you are driven by making an impact and excel in a dynamic environment, we encourage you to apply and become a valuable member of our innovative team.

In this role, you will make an impact by:

• Designing and implementing strategic change initiatives that support successful ERP and other technology transformation programs.

• Conducting stakeholder assessments, change impact assessments, and organizational readiness activities to help clients prepare for and adopt new processes and technologies.

• Developing and delivering communication, engagement, and training initiatives that drive employee adoption and business readiness throughout the transformation lifecycle.

• Supporting program leaders and business stakeholders in navigating organizational change and realizing the expected benefits of ERP implementations.

• Leveraging data-driven insights and adoption metrics to identify risks, inform decision-making, and drive successful change outcomes.

Qualifications

Whether you studied business, psychology, human resource management, political science, strategy, or something completely different, is not the most important factor to us. We are more interested in your strong analytical skills combined with an engaged, structured, and curious personality, as well as your interest in our area of expertise in Organization and Work Transformation.

We expect that you have experience delivering change management activities such as stakeholder engagement, change impact assessments, communications, training, and business readiness within complex transformation programs. In addition, you possess excellent project management and communication skills, both verbal and written, and are motivated by creating lasting value for clients and colleagues. As many of our projects are delivered in Danish organizations and involve close collaboration with local stakeholders, fluency in both Danish and English is required.

What you bring to the team:

• 1-3 years of consulting or change management experience, with experience supporting large-scale business or technology transformation programs.

• SAP change management experience preferred, with an understanding of organizational change and transformation methodologies.

• Experience in stakeholder management, communication planning, training, and user adoption activities.

• Strong presentation, facilitation, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to work effectively in client-facing environments and collaborate with diverse stakeholder groups.

• Fluency in both Danish and English is required.

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Additional Information

Do you want to be part of our team?

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your application, CV, and grade transcript by 01.11.2026. We process applications and arrange interviews continually, so we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Expected start date: 04.01.2027

Please do not hesitate to contact Karoline Gillespy, Senior Consultant at kagillespy@deloitte.dk or Anne Bach-Kristensen, Senior Consultant at annebach@deloitte.dk if you have any questions about the position.

At Deloitte, we value different skills, perspectives, and experiences, as it enables us to effectively solve complex challenges for our clients. We encourage you to apply for the position if you believe your skills can contribute to our team´s success.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

**We're looking for our 4th team member!

**Do you thrive creating structure in chaos?

Would you like to be a part of shaping the data infrastructure in a growing startup?

Does your Python code run like a well oiled machine, handling massive datasets with ease?

Then proprty.ai might be just the place for you!

**The Product

**We're building an exciting product to help property owners maintain buildings in a timely, cost-effective, and sustainable manner. We integrate public and private data sources, statistical models, and AI to deliver a modern consumer grade user experience in our app.

The software we’re building includes tools for condition assessment of individual building parts on a property, gathering public data for a building portfolio overview and creating ML & AI models for predicting remaining lifespan and forecasting maintenance cost.

The product went live in 2024, and is solving real problems for real people, and there's SO many things we can do to make it even better!

**About You

**We won't pretend there's a perfect checklist, but here's who we imagine joining us:

• You have a couple of years of professional experience building data pipelines, backend services, or similar setups.

• You take personal pride in your work. You want your work to matter.

• You're a startup type more than a corporate type: you prefer short decision paths over steering committees, you'd rather ask "why not?" than wait for a mandate, and you're comfortable when the answer to "who owns this?" is sometimes "you do, as of now".

• You create structure rather than wait for it. Ambiguity doesn't paralyze you.

**About Us

**The team consists of three people, two Data Scientists and one Data Engineer, working closely with our app team of five. We’re looking for a Backend Developer/Data Engineer to join us in developing and optimizing our data pipelines, backend services, and integrations. Most of our setup is in Databricks on Azure, using Python and SQL for the tasks.

We're expanding into Norway, the Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland, and we need more hands on creating a globalized and scalable setup for the years to come!

**The job

**Our team is creating an analytics heavy backend both serving the development and implementation of AI & ML models, and providing foundational data for our app team.

You’ll be the second in proprty.ai in this specific area of expertise and should have at least a couple of years of experience from developing similar setups.

**Your Main Responsibilities Will Be

**

• To evaluate and improve our tech-stack, database structure, and data flow.

• Creating structured data using a collection of data from multiple sources.

• Integrating new data sources in the current data flow.

• Ensuring that data pipelines run flawlessly.

• Connect our database and data science setup to both our frontend and external systems.

• Develop API integrations

• Help drive tech and AI adoption across the teams in proprty.ai

Most of the tasks above should be familiar to you.

**Location

**We're located in a beautiful historic open office space right next to Rådhuspladsen. We usually work from home on Wednesdays.

This position requires you to be in the office four days every week.

**TL;DR

**If you have opinions on creating the best data infrastructure and want to be a part of a growing team of young people on a mission to change the industry, apply now.

jobs.occupation: Opslag 170259 Professor or Associate Professor and Research Group Leader with special focus on molecular mechanisms of diabetes
jobs.description:
Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC), University of Copenhagen

   

  BRIC wishes to recruit a strongly motivated scientist at Associate Professor or Professor level for an independent research group leader position. We are seeking excellent candidates with ambitious research visions within translational diabetes type 1 or 2 research and a drive to contribute to a diverse and inspiring research environment. The research group leader position is combined with a senior researcher position at the Bartholin Institute, Department of Pathology, Centre for Diagnostics, Rigshospitalet, Capital Region. The start date is 1 April 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

  It is a requirement for the appointment that the applicant is accepted for both the research group leader position and the senior researcher position. In order to be considered, the applicant must send two applications: one to the faculty (the research group leader position) and one to the hospital (the senior researcher position) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the senior researcher position. This also applies to applicants who are already employed at the Hospital. The advertisement for the senior researcher position is available here

  The workplace
 BRIC is an international center of excellence with the mission to perform cutting-edge basic and translational biomedical research in an open environment that fosters interdisciplinarity and collaboration. Active research areas include many aspects of cancer biology, stem cell biology and neurobiology. The center is part of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. 

  Job description
 As a group leader, you will establish an independent research program within translational diabetes research. Your capacity to integrate research and clinical perspectives is emphasized. In the job, you will be expected to:

   	
• Conduct, publish, and communicate high-quality research that moves the field forward 	
• Engage in outreach and knowledge-sharing with society 	
• Develop your research group through attraction of competitive funding and talent development of team members 	
• Conduct research-based teaching and examination 	
• Be involved in academic assessments 	
• Be involved in local as well as international collaborative and multidisciplinary research projects and engage in core center activities such as talent or technology development to advance BRIC’s research environment and culture   You are also expected to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills and to contribute to developing the research environment and culture at BRIC.

  50 % of the working time is employment at Copenhagen University and will be allocated to academic tasks (e.g., research, teaching, evaluation tasks and communication with the public) in agreement with the Director at the Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC). The remaining time will be allocated for other tasks at the Bartholin Institute and the Department of Pathology (e.g. research administration, personnel responsibility, methods establishment and development, grant writing and the establishment of a competitive research group) in agreement with the Head of the Bartholin Institute.

  Candidate profile
 Your background includes a PhD degree, postdoctoral training, and a track record documenting your research experience as reflected in a strong publication record matching your career stage. Also desired is a successful record of attraction of funds, leadership and educational experiences, collaboration experiences and additional capabilities within areas such as outreach or technology transfer activities, again reflecting your career stage.  

  We offer

   	
• Access to cutting edge technologies through core facilities, including high-content screening, flow cytometry, next-gen sequencing, bioinformatics, microscopy, single cell genomics, histology and access to spatial transcriptomics and pathology services. Additional core facilities are available at faculty level. 	
• A vibrant and open scientific community with focus on collegiality, collaboration and creativity.  	
• A focus on talent training and development at all career stages, including strong PhD and postdoc programs. 	
• Strategic support for funding strategizing, grant writing and implementation of larger grants and collaborations and for research communication and outreach. 	
• A package covering the salary of 1-2 group members and technical support equivalent to 50 % of a full-time technical position from the Bartholin Institute. 	
• Administrative support with regards to laboratory services and safety, purchase, economy, HR, and IT. 	
• Additional start support may be obtained from private foundations (obtained at individual or center level).   Terms of employment
 Initial appointment as group leader (Associate Professor) is for 6 years.

  BRIC wants to offer a further career path pending a positive evaluation following transparent guidelines, which include the UCPH criteria for recognizing merit

  This can happen in form of employment in a permanent position based on public advertisement, or the group leader may enter the University of Copenhagen Promotion Program towards a position as full professor (permanent position). Experienced research leaders may be recruited at the level of full professor. 

  The average weekly working hours in the combined position are 37 hours per week.

  Salary and other terms and conditions of appointment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations. 

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

  Additional information about BRIC can be found on www.bric.ku.dk

  Inquiries are welcome to Director Anders H. Lund bric-director@bric.ku.dk

  Recruitment process
 The recruitment process will contain four evaluation steps: 

   	
• After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager will shortlist applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointment Committee after an evaluation of the written application material. Evaluation criteria can be seen here. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. Due to differences in career stage or institutional background, not all candidates are required to fulfil all requirements in full. 	
• The Vice Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. The selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee, and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. 	
• Selected candidates will be evaluated in an online interview with the Appointment committee. The online interviews is expected to be carried out between late January and early February  	
• Selected candidates will be invited for an on-site visit and final evaluation in late February    

  To be qualified for a Professor or Associate Professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion..

  You can read about the recruitment process here: Recruitment process  – University of Copenhagen.

  Application material

   	
• Cover letter outlining the applicant’s motivation to apply to BRIC and brief summaries of research visions (1 page). 	
• Application dossier (10 pages) 	 		
• Research vision/goal and synergy with BRIC 		
• Current and future research plan 		
• Description of five most significant contributions (e.g., scientific, clinical, commercial achievements, honours/awards) 		
• List of funding and commercial income raised incl. information about grant donor, type of grant, amount, and period 		
• Description of leadership experience and development. 		
• Description of organizational activities, including initiatives, responsibilities, and participation in committees and platforms 		
• Teaching portfolio including reflection on teaching and supervision, see guidelines. Selected candidates that do not have the required teaching experience will be given the opportunity to qualify within the first two years of employment. 	 	    	
• CV (2 pages use provided sub-sections) 	
• Diplomas 	
• Complete list of publications/ORCID – please indicate contribution in collaborative papers. Highlight selected publications relevant for research plan and for these include a short description (10 lines) of outcome/impact of the work and your contribution.  	
• Reprints of up to five selected papers (Associate Professor) or ten (Professor) (only published or in press)    

  Please note the level of appointment sought.

  Please note that selected applicants who have applied for either both positions or just the professor position will be assessed for the associate professor position if they are found not-qualified for the professor position.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the Assessment Committee requires further documentation. The Assessment Committee is comprised of employees from both BRIC and Rigshospitalet.
 
 The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. 
 
 The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested applicants to apply for this position (see also https://www.bric.ku.dk/career-at-bric)
 
 Please submit the application with the required attachments. The closing date for applications is 23.59 p.m. CET, Thursday, 19 November 2026

  BRIC highly values diversity and encourages people of all backgrounds to apply see also https://www.bric.ku.dk/career-at-bric

  The University of Copenhagen International Staff Mobility Office offers assistance and guidance regarding relocation, e.g., housing, spouse program, pension and taxes, as well as on general information on the Danish society, e.g. child-care, healthcare etc. For more information, visit the ISM website:  https://ism.ku.dk/.

Consultant Interventional Cardiologist – PCI On-Call Service

Department of Cardiology, Aalborg University Hospital, Denmark

The opportunity
Are you an experienced interventional cardiologist looking to join a highly specialised university hospital with a strong clinical, academic and collaborative environment?

The Department of Cardiology at Aalborg University Hospital is seeking one or more Consultant Interventional Cardiologists from the EU/EØS to join our team. We welcome applications from candidates who are already qualified to participate in a PCI on-call service, as well as experienced PCI operators who are motivated to develop the additional competencies required for on-call duties.

The position is available as soon as possible or by mutual agreement.

This is an opportunity to work in a busy interventional cardiology environment, contribute to the development of specialised cardiac care and collaborate with highly skilled colleagues across cardiology, cardiac surgery and other disciplines.

The position

everyone else get more out of what they already use, at the right cost. A patch here and a small workflow there won't cut it. You'll get into every department, find what should be built, and build it, while communicating priorities and tradeoffs to the team.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in computational modeling of visual perception
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a fully funded postdoctoral position in computational modeling of visual perception. The position is available for up to 36 months and is part of a project led by Dr. Gregory Scott Francis that is supported by the SDU Department of Psychology. The starting date is March 15, 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Research environment

The postdoc will be affiliated with the Research Unit of Health and Cognitive Psychology. The position is at the SDU Esbjerg campus but will also involve interaction with staff at the SDU Odense campus. 

Project description

A basic process of the visual system is to monitor the location and characteristics of objects in a scene, and the multiple object tracking (MOT) paradigm has identified many fundamental aspects of this process. With a rich literature of empirical results, this paradigm is ready for theoretical development, which this project intends to pursue using an integrate-and-fire neural network model known as LAMINART. A key aspect of the model is the ability to select/segment visual objects, which may explain how people can (seemingly) effortlessly track multiple objects in a dynamic visual scene. 

The successful candidate will be required to design, program and analyze an integrate-and-fire neural network model of visual perception. Good programming (Python) skills are required along with a good understanding of empirical methods and ways to connect empirical findings with model behavior. The position also involves teaching duties.

The project involves collaboration with Prof. Søren Krogh Andersen, also at SDU.

Qualifications

Ideally, applicants for the position should satisfy the following requirements:

• 
PhD level in psychology, cognitive (neuro)science, vision science, or a related field

• 
Research experience as evidenced by conference contributions and peer-reviewed journal articles in a field related to the offered position

• 
Expertise in visual attention and perception

• 
Strong analytical skills, including the ability to design, implement, and analyze complex experiments

• 
Be willing and able to teach for the Department of Psychology

• 
Prior experience with neural network modeling is a plus

• 
Prior experience with cognitive modelling is a plus

• 
Good command of statistics

• 
Good command of Python (or similar programming languages and a willingness to learn)

• 
Very good command of the English language in spoken and written form

• 
Some knowledge of the Danish language is a plus

Candidates who are about to obtain these qualifications are also encouraged to apply. 

Contact information

For further information about the position, please contact Dr. Greg Francis, SDU (email: gfrancis@health.sdu.dk; phone: +45 65 50 16 98), or Professor Søren Krogh Andersen (email: skandersen@health.sdu.dk; phone: +45 65 50 49 57)

Application deadline

The application deadline is November 08, 2026, at 23.59 hrs. CET.

Salary and terms of employment

The base salary for a postdoctoral researcher is DKK 36,877.42, with an additional job structure supplement of DKK 5,230.75. This brings the total monthly salary to DKK 42,108.16.

The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Application

Applications must be in English and submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". 

Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format.

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

The application must include (as PDF files) (please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total):

• 
A letter of motivation (max. 1 page)

• 
A detailed CV

• 
Master and PhD degree certificates, if available

• 
A complete and numbered list of publications 

• 
Three scientific publications (or preprints) considered to be most important for the advertised position (please note that one file per publication must be submitted)

• 
Contact details of at least two university supervisors or employers who can provide references

If you experience technical problems, you must contact hcm-support@sdu.dk.

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application. 

Incomplete applications and applications received after the application deadline will not be considered. 

Shortlisting of applications may be used in the initial selection process.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.
